primitives.name: Deterministic Cross-Branch Inventory Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: # NOVA Multi-Head Convergence Inventory Deterministic cross-branch inventory produced by `scripts/nova/multihead-inventory.mjs`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'set of branch heads', 'B': 'base commit SHA', 'C': 'collision status flag'}
primitives.assumptions: All branches are deterministic under fixed base commit; collision scan is exhaustive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C = true, symbolic overlap detected in guarded symbols.

layer2.mapping: Maps Git commit graph to symbolic state space; each head corresponds to a distinct kernel state in GSI.

primitives.name: Cross-Head Symbol Collision Guard
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'symbol identifier', 'H_i': 'head branch index', 'D(S, H_i)': 'definition divergence of S in H_i'}
primitives.assumptions: Symbol definitions must be consistent across all heads to avoid runtime errors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ∃ i,j: D(S, H_i) ≠ D(S, H_j), collision occurs.

layer2.mapping: Derives symbolic kernel inconsistency from multi-head definitions; used by GSE to enforce runtime coherence.
layer2.telemetry: Number of guarded symbols with divergent definitions.

primitives.name: Prisma Schema Divergence Kernel
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'prisma schema definition', 'M': 'migration set', 'D(P, H_i)': 'schema divergence in head H_i'}
primitives.assumptions: Schema changes must be synchronized across all heads to maintain data integrity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ∃ i,j: D(P, H_i) ≠ D(P, H_j), divergence detected.

layer2.mapping: Encodes prisma schema inconsistencies as kernel-level anomalies; GSE uses this to validate migration paths.
layer2.telemetry: Count of prisma schema divergences per head.

The prisma divergence kernel extends this to schema-level inconsistencies, enabling GSE to detect and prevent data model conflicts during runtime. These operators form a dual structure: one for symbolic consistency and another for schema integrity, both rooted in the base commit state.
